thesis_triggers.event: Revised 2026-10-30 from $70 to $55, and at the citation gate 2026-11-02 to $47: with zero value for the foundry, Products at 18x NTM EBIT (~$19.9B for Nov-26..Oct-27 in the build) plus All other, less capitalised corporate cost, less SBC capitalised at the same 18x (~$2.47B NTM, -$8.1 a share, now carried because the 22.4x peer median expenses SBC) and the $16.6B NCI, plus $3.9B net cash, is ~$51 a share (~$59 before the SBC part; ~$68 in the base round before the client reset). Below ~$47 (the same ~7% cushion under that floor as before) the market would be valuing Intel Products itself under that multiple, i.e. pricing a further leg down in server pricing or share, not only the foundry. The old $70 level was broken on 2026-10-30 (close $65.76) on the Q4 guide; the evidence that moved it is the lower Products earnings in the build and the SBC basis, not the price.

supervisor_summary: Update 2026-10-30 after the Q3 print: the first standard model values INTC at $82.23, the research target (12m), vs $96 in the base round and the $65.76 close on 2026-10-30 (upside +25%). The Q4 guide resets client (CCPG down more than 20% q/q, PC TAM -12% 2026 and ~-10% 2027) and adds the Fab 28 hit, while DCAI keeps growing. At the citation gate the P/E leg was put on one basis: the peers' Zacks consensus expenses SBC, so INTC's own multiple is 47.3x, the exit 40.7x, and model EPS and the SOTP carry SBC as a cost. No 14A customer is named yet and the foundry option stays at $115B. Downside P10 $43.40, upside P90 $125.91; thesis break $47.
